Subject: Post-signature implementation plan: MAP + evaluation timeline

Hi Ben / Team,

Thanks again for getting the contract over the finish line — excited to get started. Attached is the Solstice draft MAP (MAP_Solstice_RevA.xlsx) and an initial evaluation plan we use to validate model behavior in a production lane. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm a 1-week canary window where we run traffic at 5-10% and validate latency/quality metrics.
- A migration weekend for full cutover (we prefer a Saturday).
- Two training sessions for product owners / support (one admin, one ops).
- Clarify rollback triggers and success criteria for the evaluation plan.

Can you propose dates for the canary and migration windows? We’d like the evaluation metrics (latency P95, token-accuracy proxy, and false-positive rate on our test prompts) to be finalized ahead of canary.

I copied Sanjay (our implementation lead) — he’ll own the internal resource confirmations.

Thanks,
Emily Ross
Director, Product Operations
SolsticeHealth

Subject: Re: Post-signature implementation plan: MAP + evaluation timeline

Hi Emily — great to meet you here and congrats to the teams.

Summary response and proposal:

- Canary week: Aug 18–22 (Mon–Fri). We’ll route 10% of production requests to the new model variant and run automated evals daily.
- Migration (cutover) window: Saturday Aug 30, 2200–0200 PT (4-hour planned cutover, with a 4-hour monitoring tail).
- Training: two live sessions (Aug 25 — Admin/Integration overview; Aug 26 — Support ops + runbook walk-through). We’ll record both.
- Evaluation metrics we propose to lock down pre-canary: latency P95 <= 180ms, token cost delta <= +12%, and eval-set semantic drift < 3% (per your test suite).
- Rollback triggers: sustained latency P95 > 300ms for 10 minutes OR semantic drift > 6% across a 1-hour window OR >1% increase in critical-failure prompts.

I attached an internal version of the MAP with owners and checkpoints (MAP_Solstice_RevA_for_Redwood.xlsx) and a short canary checklist. Laura will own the runbook and Neha will coordinate the eval harness and instrumentation.

Next steps (short):
1) Emily/Sanjay — confirm the canary/migration dates work for internal ops.
2) Ben/Neha — confirm instrumentation hooks (traces + token-level cost export) by Aug 8.
3) Laura — share runbook draft by Aug 6.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding a few operational details and outstanding asks from Security/Compliance: 

- Runbook outline (will deliver Aug 6): preparatory steps, pre-canary smoke tests, canary gating checklist, rollback procedures, and post-cutover verification.
- Security asks: Solstice requested SOC2 evidence and a short data-flow diagram. I’ve started the security questionnaire; can you Emily confirm who will be the contact for evidence collection? I’ll attach what we can share.
- Data handling during canary: We must ensure PII-masking is active for test traffic and that logs are routed to the customer-managed retention bucket in their VPC for the canary batch. Sanjay — please confirm that’s acceptable.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a staged ramp within the canary week: Mon 1%, Tue 2.5%, Wed 5%, Thu 7.5%, Fri 10% (and daily checkpoints).
- Neha — we’ll need the eval harness to produce a daily report (drift, latency, token-cost, top-20 failing prompts).
